name: Clobazam
meta: Psychotropic substance under the NDPS Act, 1985 and Schedule H/H1 of the Drugs &
sections: White crystalline powder, slightly soluble in water.

Synthesised in 1966 and first published in 1969; initially used for anxiety and later established as an add-on antiepileptic. First approval/introduction: Australia 1970, France 1974 (Hoechst / Roussel); US FDA 2011 for Lennox–Gastaut syndrome.

Positive allosteric modulator of GABA-A receptors, increasing chloride-channel opening frequency. 1,5-substitution gives relatively less sedation than 1,4-benzodiazepines. Receptor / target profile: Positive allosteric modulator of GABA-A receptors with relatively higher affinity for alpha-2 than alpha-1 subunits, giving anxiolytic/anticonvulsant effect with less sedation.
Summary: Bioavailability ~87%; Tmax 0.5–4 h. ~85% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP3A4 to active N-desmethylclobazam (via CYP2C19). Half-life 36–42 h (metabolite 71–82 h).
Adjunctive therapy of epilepsy (partial and generalised seizures), including Lennox–Gastaut syndrome
Short-term treatment of acute anxiety (≤2–4 weeks)
Epilepsy (adults): 20–30 mg/day initially, up to 60 mg/day; single bedtime dose or divided
Children ≥3 years: 5 mg/day initially; maintenance 0.3–1 mg/kg/day
Anxiety: 20–30 mg/day in divided doses or single bedtime dose
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Start low (5 mg/day) in mild–moderate impairment; avoid severe.
Lennox–Gastaut ≥2 years: <30 kg 5 mg/day → max 20 mg; >30 kg 10 mg/day → max 40 mg.
Avoid especially in first trimester and late pregnancy (floppy infant, withdrawal).
Dependence and withdrawal – avoid abrupt cessation
Opioids – profound sedation, respiratory depression, death
CYP2C19 inhibitors (fluconazole, omeprazole) raise metabolite levels
Hormonal contraceptives may have reduced efficacy
With or without food; avoid alcohol.
Sedation; respiratory status with opioids; skin reactions; dependence signs.
Somnolence, confusion, ataxia, respiratory depression, coma. Supportive care; flumazenil with caution (may precipitate seizures).
CONTAIN (Ng et al., Neurology 2011) – clobazam significantly reduced drop seizures in Lennox–Gastaut syndrome.
Do not stop suddenly – seizures may recur
Avoid alcohol and driving if drowsy
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
